features.title: Tour of the Configure screen
features.summary: What you will see, top to bottom, when you build an agent on the Configure tab. Use it as a map before you start.
steps: Two tabs sit at the top: Configure to build, Preview to test.
Instructions: write what the agent does, its tone and its rules. Suggest improvements asks Copilot to tighten your text.
Skills: select Add to give the agent a packaged skill. The two Skills cards on this tab explain how to add one and how to create a new one.

Knowledge: select Add knowledge, or drop files onto the box. Under Work content you can switch Cloud files (your OneDrive and SharePoint files), Outlook and Teams on or off. Copilot connectors has its own switch.
Web search is a separate switch. By default it is off. Where your organisation blocks public websites it shows a warning, and agents cannot use public URLs as knowledge.
Attachments lets you add files. Suggested prompts lets you add title and message pairs. The screen shows three rows to start with.
limits: Seen in a live work tenant on 5 November 2026, where web search was blocked and Copilot connectors were off. Your screen may differ with your licence, admin settings and app version.
Which knowledge sources you can use depends on your licence. See the licence card on this tab.

source.label: Seen in a live work tenant, 5 Nov 2026

features.title: Stage 1: Create an agent
features.summary: Agent Builder is the simple tool inside Microsoft 365 Copilot for building your own agent. You can describe the agent in plain words, fill in a form, or start from a template.
steps: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot (microsoft365.com/chat, office.com/chat or the Teams desktop or web app) and select New agent.
To describe it: type what you want on the Describe tab. Copilot fills in the name, description and instructions for you.
To fill it in yourself: select Skip to configure to open the Configure tab.
To save time: under Start with a template, pick a template. The agent is created for you.
When it is ready, select Create. The agent is private to you until you share it.
prompts: Create an agent that summarises my daily emails and includes attachments.
Create an agent that helps new starters in my team find onboarding information.
Update the agent to summarise Teams chats instead of emails.
limits: Not available on mobile versions of the apps and sites (Agent Builder overview page).
The Describe (natural language) experience only works if your Microsoft 365 language is on the supported list. Otherwise use Configure.
Name: 30 characters. Description: 1,000 characters.

source.label: Build agents in Agent Builder (Microsoft Learn)

features.title: Stage 2: Write the instructions
features.summary: Instructions tell the agent what its job is and how to do it. If you use the Describe tab, Copilot writes them for you. You can then edit them on the Configure tab.
steps: Open the agent and go to the Configure tab.
Find the Instructions box. Read what Copilot wrote if you used Describe.
State the job, the steps, and how the answer should look.
Add one or two examples of a good answer.
Test on the Try it tab and edit again.
prompts: Paste this into Instructions (example): You are the Team Onboarding Buddy. Help new starters in my team. Answer only from the knowledge sources I have added. Steps: 1) Ask which role the person has if they have not said. 2) Give a short checklist of what to do in week one. 3) Point to the document the answer came from. Keep answers under 150 words, in plain UK English, with short bullet points. If the answer is not in the sources, say 'I could not find that' and suggest who to ask. Never guess.
Make my instructions shorter and clearer.
Add an example answer to the instructions.
limits: Instructions: 8,000 characters maximum.
Description: 1,000 characters. It helps Copilot pick your agent, so keep it short and precise.

source.label: Build agents in Agent Builder (Microsoft Learn)

features.title: Stage 3: Add knowledge sources
features.summary: Knowledge is the material the agent answers from. You can add SharePoint and OneDrive content, files from your device, public websites, Teams chats and meetings, email and connectors.
steps: On the Configure tab, find the Knowledge section.
Select Add knowledge, or drop files onto the box.
Under Work content, switch on or off Cloud files (your OneDrive and SharePoint files), Outlook and Teams. Each shows a Search all label when it is on.
Copilot connectors has its own switch. It is often off, so ask your admin if you need it.
Web search is a separate switch. By default it is off, and where your organisation blocks public websites it shows a warning and agents cannot use public URLs as knowledge.
Use Attachments to add files for the agent to read.
Wait if a file shows Preparing. The agent will not use it until it is ready.
prompts: Use only the files in my team's onboarding folder to answer questions.
Add this SharePoint site as a source and answer from it first.
What does the holiday policy say about carrying over leave?
limits: Seen in a live work tenant on 5 November 2026. Button names can differ by app version and admin settings.
Per agent: 4 public website URLs, 100 SharePoint files, 1 SharePoint list, 50 OneDrive files, 5 Teams chats and 5 meetings, 20 uploaded files.
Web addresses can be two levels deep at most and cannot contain query parameters.
The agent respects each person's permissions. If a user cannot open a file, the agent will not use it for them.
Embedded file size limits: 512 MB for Word, PDF, PowerPoint and text files, 30 MB for Excel files. If Restricted SharePoint Search is on, SharePoint cannot be a knowledge source.

source.label: Add knowledge sources to an agent in Agent Builder (Microsoft Learn)

features.title: Stage 4: Test on the Preview tab
features.summary: Try it is a live copy of your agent inside the builder. Ask real questions, check the answers against your sources, and keep editing until it behaves.
steps: Give the agent a name, description and instructions. Try it only turns on once these exist.
Select the Preview tab at the top. Some Microsoft pages call it Try it.
Select a suggested prompt or type your own question.
Check the answer matches the source. Use the thumbs up or down on the reply to send feedback.
Select New chat to start again, then change instructions or knowledge and retest.
prompts: What should I do in my first week?
Where did that answer come from?
Ask something your sources do not cover, to check the agent says it cannot find it.
limits: Some features do not work in Try it, such as sharing prompts, feedback on the agent itself, and @mentioning other agents. Use them after you create the agent.
Newly uploaded SharePoint or OneDrive files show Preparing and are ignored until ready.

source.label: Build agents in Agent Builder (Microsoft Learn)

features.title: Stage 5: Share your agent
features.summary: Sharing gives named people or groups direct access to your agent. You choose who can chat and who can edit. Your admin may have turned off sharing with everyone in the organisation, so plan to share with named people or groups.
steps: Select Create. A message confirms the agent is private to you.
Select Share to open the share dialog.
In Add a name, group, or email, enter the people or group.
Set the role: Can chat (use only) or Can edit (owner). Leave Send notification ticked if you want them emailed.
Select Add. You can also use Copy chat link.
prompts: Share the chat link with my team and ask them to try three questions.
Make my colleague a Can edit owner so we can maintain it together.
After editing, select Update so shared users see the changes.
limits: In a live work tenant on 5 November 2026 the admin had turned off sharing an agent with everyone in the organisation. You can still share with named people or groups.
A group can only be added as Can chat. Add people one by one to make them owners.
Your admin may limit who can share, or turn off Org-wide sharing for chat access. Choices are all users (default), specific users or groups, or no users.
People need the right Copilot licence for the agent's capabilities, or they may see an error.
SharePoint files you added are only shared automatically when you share with specific security groups, not everyone in the organisation (Agent Builder overview page, known limitations).

source.label: Share and manage agents built in Agent Builder (Microsoft Learn)

features.title: Publish to your organisation's catalogue
features.summary: To make an agent findable by everyone at work, submit it to your org catalogue. An admin reviews it and, if approved, lists it under Built by your org in the Agent Store.
steps: Go to All agents, pick your agent and select Edit. Select Update if there are unpublished changes.
Select the More ellipses (...) and then Submit to your org catalog.
Fill in Display name, Short description, Developer name, Creator website, Privacy statement and Terms of use.
Select Continue. The dialog shows Submitted for admin approval.
Check the status later: Waiting for approval, Approved, or Rejected by your admin.
prompts: Short description example (80 characters max): Answers new starter questions from our onboarding pages.
If your agent reads personal email or Teams chats, say so in the short description.
After approval, open All agents, find your agent under Built by your org, and copy its link.
limits: The menu item is disabled until you have published the agent at least once.
Display name: 30 characters. Short description: 80 characters. Developer name: 32 characters.
Later edits only reach the Agent Store after you resubmit and an admin approves.

source.label: Submit agents from Agent Builder to your org catalog (Microsoft Learn)

features.title: Skills: what they are and how to add one
features.summary: A skill is a packaged, repeatable task for the agent. It is a folder with a SKILL.md file of instructions, plus optional files and scripts. You can ask Agent Builder to create one, or upload a .zip.
steps: Open Agent Builder and go to the Configure tab.
Find the Skills section, which says Add skills to specialise this agent. Expand it and select Add.
Upload the complete .zip skill package. Do not upload SKILL.md on its own.
Review the skill name, description, instructions and files.
Select the Preview tab and ask a question that should use the skill.
prompts: Use the weekly update skill on these notes.
Which skill did you just use, and why?
limits: Up to 8 skills per agent. Each .zip is up to 50 MB, with up to 25 MB per file, 350 files in total and folders no deeper than 3 levels. Skill instructions must be under 20,000 characters.
Skill scripts run in a sandbox with no internet access and no package installs. Skills cannot be reused across agents.

Microsoft's pages do not say whether skills are in preview or generally available (checked 2026-11-05), so check with your admin. If your tenant uses Purview Information Barriers, end users cannot add skills.
Seen on the Configure tab of a live work tenant on 5 November 2026: a Skills section with an Add button.

source.label: Add skills to your declarative agent in Agent Builder (Microsoft Learn) and Skills in declarative agents

features.title: Create a new skill
features.summary: A skill is a saved routine the agent follows the same way every time. There are two ways to make one: ask Agent Builder to write it, or build the package yourself.
steps: Way 1, describe it. In Copilot chat select Agents & Skills, then New agent. In the Message Agent Builder box, describe the routine and ask for a reusable skill.
On the Configure tab, open Skills and check a skill was created. Select it to review the details.
If it was not added, use Way 2.

Way 2, build the package. Make a folder with a file named SKILL.md. At the top of SKILL.md put a name and a description between two lines of three dashes (this is called YAML front matter). Below that write the instructions, under 20,000 characters.
Add optional files such as templates or a script. Zip the whole folder.
On Configure, expand Skills, select Add and upload the .zip. Then test it on the Preview tab.
prompts: Create an agent that helps my team write release notes. Add a reusable skill that always follows the same steps: group the changes into Features, Fixes and Other, then format a clean Markdown changelog with a version heading and today's date.

---
name: weekly-update
description: Turns rough notes into our standard weekly update. Use when someone asks for a weekly update.
---
Write the update in three parts: Done this week, Next week, Risks. Keep each part to five bullets. Use plain words. Ask me for anything missing before you write.
limits: Up to 8 skills per agent. The .zip can be up to 50 MB, with up to 25 MB per file, 350 files in total, and folders no deeper than 3 levels.
Scripts run in a sandbox with no internet and no package installs. A skill cannot be reused across agents, so upload it again for each agent.
The first prompt is Microsoft's own example. The SKILL.md example is ours, to show the layout. Change the wording to fit your work.
Microsoft's pages do not say whether skills are preview or generally available (checked 2026-11-05). If your tenant uses Purview Information Barriers, end users cannot add skills.

source.label: Add skills in Agent Builder and Skills in declarative agents (Microsoft Learn, updated 26 Oct 2026)

features.title: Who can build, and what your licence allows
features.summary: What you can add depends on your licence. Admins can also switch Agent Builder on or off and control sharing. Check this before you promise a colleague an agent.
steps: Check you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. It unlocks all knowledge sources.
If Agent Builder is missing, ask your admin. They can control whether it is available.
If Org-wide sharing for chat access is greyed out, an admin policy is limiting it.
Ask your admin about agent controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
prompts: Ask your admin: Is Agent Builder turned on for me?
Ask your admin: Can I use Org-wide sharing, or must I share with named people?
Ask your admin: Which knowledge sources and connectors are enabled for us?
limits: With a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence: web search, connectors, SharePoint, uploaded files, Dataverse, email, people, Teams messages and meetings are all listed as available.
Without a Copilot licence but with Copilot Chat: web search only. SharePoint, files and connectors need pay-as-you-go billing. Email, people and Teams need the full licence.
Agents in Agent Builder do not use your tenant's Dataverse storage, and Customer Managed Keys are not supported.

source.label: Agent capabilities and licensing models (Microsoft Learn)

features.title: Build your first agent: a Team Onboarding Buddy
features.summary: A worked example from start to finish. You will describe an agent, point it at one SharePoint folder, test it and share it with your team.
steps: Select New agent. On the Describe tab, type the first prompt below.
Open the Configure tab. Under Knowledge, use Enter URL or Browse to add your team's onboarding folder.
Paste the example instructions from Stage 2 into Instructions. Turn on Only use specified sources.
Select Try it and ask the test questions. Fix anything wrong, then select Create.
Select Share, add your team as Can chat, and select Add.
prompts: Create an agent called Team Onboarding Buddy that helps new starters in my team find what they need in their first week.
What do I need to do on my first day?
Who do I ask about expenses?
What is the capital of Mars? (a check that it admits when the answer is not in your sources)
limits: Name is capped at 30 characters.
Make sure your team can open the folder. The agent only uses files the person asking is allowed to see.
Test with real questions before sharing. Agents can still get things wrong, so keep a human check on anything important.

source.label: Build agents in Agent Builder (Microsoft Learn)

issues.text: Agent Builder cannot author actions that connect to outside services. To add actions, connectors or workflows, copy the agent to Copilot Studio.
Agents built in Agent Builder cannot be used in Teams group or 1:1 chats.

Colleagues who cannot open the SharePoint files you added will not get answers from them. Auto-sharing of those files only works when you share with specific security groups, not everyone. If it fails, the agent is still shared and the file owner must grant access in SharePoint. Also, the Web content toggle stays on screen even when an admin has blocked web search, and the admin policy wins.
